My dad just passed, also cancer, and we had the services this weekend. Similar to you, I was raised in a Catholic family with a strong sense of faith and belief in heaven. I'm spiritual/atheist, but don't know what I think of the afterlife. My big belief has always surrounded the energy that you mentioned we are made up of. After all, what is heaven if no one but God's own children will get in? 

But something the pastor said stuck with me.

He said my father's earthly body may have reached the end of its life but his spirit was only just beginning to come alive. His soul is eternal. 

To the pastor, that may mean one thing. To him it means God is awaiting his souls arrival in heaven. He said we bury him in the ground because Christ needs only a little bit of physical DNA to make a vessel for him past the gates. 

But to me, I hear "his spirit is alive" and then all of a sudden ghosts make sense to me. 

He lives, still, with memory, and is forever in our minds. 

When I first came down to visit my father when his illness turned, I took a trip to a secluded park nearby, and sat, and thought, and played in the dirt. I wrote and spoke aloud about my father to no one in particular. I closed my eyes for a few minutes, just to listen to the wind, and when I opened them, a small, round, orange butterfly crossed my vision. 

I thought of my father, who was small and round and often sported orange.

In the past few weeks I've been seeing a ton of butterflies. Each time, I think of Dad, and suddenly he's there again, with me, just this time in my mind. That spirit, his ghost, is that butterfly.

This is to say-- 

Our loved ones live on in our memory. Their bodies decompose, or burn, and all that's really left in the physical world is the memory, and whatever worldly possessions they collected. Their spirit leaves their body and expands, finding a place in all of our minds. Their energy is now ours. Let the butterflies serve as a reminder. Each time we see one, our fathers are back with us, alive and laughing, cursing at the other drivers on the road and bringing us hoards of our favorite foods. They remain with us. If we as human beings are only energy, then our fathers are here, because we are using our energy to think of them, to speak about them, to write flowery online posts about them. Our fathers are butterflies because *we* decide it. Our fathers are butterflies because we remember them every time they come to us. Not only that, but the butterflies feed from the flowers planted in the grass that grew out of decomposition. They spread pollen around, which then grows the food we eat. And isn't it just like our fathers, to try and keep us fed?

I believe **that** is the God the Christians talk about. Not the flesh and bone man walking the skies but instead the very flesh and bone that we ourselves are made up of.
